title: Heterogeneous precision routing + KV placement proposal
content:
Purpose and context:
This doc proposes a concrete execution path and KV-cache placement strategy for mixed-precision serving (INT8, FP8, GPTQ, AWQ) that minimizes cross-kernel data movement, preserves kv-cache coherency, and allows graceful precision fallbacks when hardware or kernel availability changes. Aim is to spell out: routing decisions, per-request annotations, in-memory layout for cached keys/values across precision variants, scheduler handoff rules, and safety/telemetry hooks for regressions.

Motivation / problems we see today:
- When a request hits a model with mixed-precision variants (e.g., FP8 baseline, INT8 optimized kernels, GPTQ for large layers), we often pay serialization/deserialization costs converting kv-cache blocks between kernel representations.
- Current scheduler treats precision as a per-model static property; this prevents opportunistic routing to faster kernels (e.g., AWQ on certain layers) without full cache rebuilds.
- KV cache eviction and placement are naive. When we run heterogeneous precision kernels on the same serving node, we duplicate cache entries or pay conversion time.
- Observed tail latency spikes when fallback kernels are chosen mid-sequence because of on-the-fly cache conversions.

Guiding principles:
1) Avoid duplicate persistent copies of KV state for the same logical sequence unless necessary for correctness.
2) Enable incremental, lazy conversion of KV tiles at kernel handoff time where conversion cost < recompute cost.
3) Keep scheduler decisions deterministic and replayable: record per-request precision annotations to traceability layer.
4) Prefer in-place compatible kernel interfaces so caching layer can share memory where safe.

Key definitions (informal):
- tile: contiguous block of K/V for a subset of heads/time-steps.
- precision-zone: contiguous set of layers or tiles served by the same precision/kernels (e.g., first 12 layers FP8, next 12 AWQ).
- representation: serialized in-memory layout of a tile for a kernel (formats differ between GPTQ-packed, AWQ-blocks, INT8-symmetric).

Proposal overview (high-level):
- Per-request precision policy: Each incoming request carries a precision_preference: [primary, fallback_list]. Primary is the preferred runtime. Fallback_list is ordered. Example: [AWQ, INT8, FP8, FP32].
- Precision-aware routing phase (router): Using request policy + node health + kernel availability, pick target kernel per precision-zone. Router emits a per-request routing plan (per layer range) that is persisted in the request metadata and stamped into logs/traces.
- KV storage model: store tiles in a canonical on-disk/in-memory canonical_layout chosen at load time (default: FP32-friendly layout). For each tile we maintain a small descriptor: {tile_id, logical_seq, current_representation, last_converted_at, refcount}. Representations can be: canonical_fp32, variant_awq_block, variant_gptq_packed, variant_int8_tile.
- Conversion strategy: lazy, tile-level conversion. When kernel X needs a tile in its representation and tile is not present, convert from the nearest available representation. Conversion costs are profiled offline and stored in catalog. Use heuristics: if conversion_time < expected remaining generation_time for the request, convert; else route to fallback kernel.

Kernel handoff rules (scheduler side):
- Handoff occurs at layer boundaries defined in the routing plan. At handoff:
  - Mark warmup flag for new kernel and prefetch next N tiles (configurable; default N=2 layers).
  - If tile representation exists in-memory compatible with kernel ABI -> direct use.
  - Else attempt async conversion: spawn conversion task in local worker pool with priority = request_priority. If conversion completes within tile_deadline -> proceed. If not, evaluate fallback in routing_plan.
- Deterministic ordering: conversion tasks must be scheduled FIFO per-request to preserve deterministic state when replaying.

KV eviction and placement strategy:
- Per-node per-model segment store with eviction tiers: hot (recently used tiles), warm (converted copies with refcount=0 but retained), cold (can be dropped).
- When memory pressure triggers eviction, prefer dropping non-canonical converted variants first, then cold canonical entries.
- When model pinned to dedicated node pool, privilege keeping canonical copies.

Telemetry and safety hooks:
- Emit events: routing_plan_created, tile_conversion_started/finished/failed, handoff_started/finished, fallback_invoked. Each event includes request_id, tile_id(s), from_representation, to_representation, conversion_ms, kernel_version, node_id.
- Track metrics: conversion_rate, average_conversion_latency, conversion_failures, fallback_rate, duplicate_kv_memory_overhead.
- Safety: if conversion_failures for request > 1 or fallback_rate spikes > threshold (configurable), route subsequent traffic for that model to conservative precision (e.g., FP32) and alert SRE.

Performance modeling and catalog data required:
- For each kernel variant: average per-tile conversion time from every other representation -> matrix conver_time[rep_from][rep_to].
- Per-kernel per-token generation throughput and latency by sequence length distribution.
- Memory delta for keeping converted variants.

Experiment plan (short):
1) Canary: implement router that emits routing_plan and simple logging (no conversion) to collect kernel availability and warmup patterns over 2 weeks for a set of customer workloads.
2) Conversion POC: implement tile-level lazy conversion for AWQ<->canonical_fp32 and measure overhead on internal bench. Use small model (e.g., 7B) traffic and synthetic seq lengths.
3) Scheduler integration: add conversion task queue with priority and timeouts. Run A/B vs current baseline.
4) Gradual rollout: enable conversions in canary nodes, monitor telemetry, enable automatic fallback thresholds.

Open questions / discussion items:
- Do we need a stricter notion of canonical representation per-model family? (e.g., LLaMA-family canonical=fp32 vs Falcon canonical=fp16)
- Is tile-level conversion granular enough for extremely wide heads (32k head-dim)? We may need sub-tile (chunk) conversions.
- Should conversion be checkpointed to persistent local disk to avoid repeated conversion across restarts? Pros/cons: avoids repeated CPU cost vs persists potentially large data on nodes.
- How will multi-tenant nodes handle refcounts across models and isolation concerns?

Implementation TODOs (owner assignments):
- router: emit per-request routing_plan schema (Priya)
- tile descriptor store: in-memory store + metrics (Evan)
- conversion library: AWQ<->canonical, GPTQ->canonical, INT8 shim (Maya)
- scheduler hooks: handoff & conversion task queue (Jonah)
- telemetry events and dashboards (Priya + SRE)

Immediate next steps:
- Review with serving-runtime team (this week) and get buy-in on per-request routing_plan format.
- Spike work: MVP conversion lib for AWQ; measure conversion latency across nodes (2 weeks).
- Document storage format for tile descriptors and prototype evictor logic.

Notes to self / rough reminders:
- Keep conversions opt-in per-model until we have robust telemetry.
- Consider adding a small LRU compress cache for converted variants to limit memory blowup.
- When in doubt pick deterministic fallback path vs optimistic conversion.

References / links:
- RI-1428 (Jira): work item for per-request routing metadata
- runtime PR #361: initial scheduler hook prototype

Unresolved: prioritize sub-tile conversions vs whole-tile conversions for GPTQ. Schedule follow-up meeting with research team to scope quant packing formats (Maya + Research).

End of draft.
